title: U.S. House · North Carolina's 3rd District
area: Eastern North Carolina, including Greenville and the Outer Banks.

context.text: Raymond Smith Jr. defeated Allison Jaslow 56.7%-43.3% in the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary. Incumbent Gregory Murphy (R) advanced from a canceled Republican primary and faces Smith and Libertarian Daniel Cavender in the general election.

candidates.name: Gregory Murphy

summary.text: Gregory Murphy is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in North Carolina's 3rd Congressional District. A urologic surgeon and former state legislator, he served in the North Carolina House from 2015 to 2019 and has represented the district in Congress since a 2019 special election. He serves on the House Ways and Means, Veterans' Affairs, and House Administration committees.

background.text: Born in Raleigh, North Carolina, where he grew up; graduated magna cum laude from Davidson College in 1985.

Earned his medical degree from the University of North Carolina School of Medicine, graduating with honors and as a member of Alpha Omega Alpha, then completed a surgical residency in urology and renal transplantation at the University of Kentucky.

Practiced as a urologist in Greenville, North Carolina; his official biography says he was president of Eastern Urological Associates, an affiliate professor of surgery and chief of the Division of Urology at the East Carolina University School of Medicine, and chief of staff of Vidant Medical Center for three years.

According to his official biography, has served as a medical missionary on trips to countries including India, Nicaragua, Haiti, and several in Africa, and was Davidson College's alumni president and a member of its board of trustees.

Served in the North Carolina House of Representatives, District 9, from 2015 to 2019; his official biography says he was Senior Chair of Health Policy and Chair of Health and Human Services Appropriations and was primary author of the STOP Act and HOPE Act, state opioid-response measures.
Won the July 9, 2019 Republican primary runoff over Joan Perry in the special election to succeed the late Rep. Walter B. Jones Jr., and was sworn into the U.S. House on September 15, 2019.

Serves on the House Ways and Means Committee (Health and Trade subcommittees), the Veterans' Affairs Committee (Health Subcommittee), and the Committee on House Administration (Oversight Subcommittee).
Co-chairs the House Republican Doctors Caucus and the Academic Medicine Caucus, and describes himself as the only actively practicing physician in Congress.

priorities.text: Expanding school choice so parents can choose the best educational path for their children, whether traditional public, private, charter, online school, or homeschooling.
An "all-of-the-above" energy policy using traditional and clean energy sources to improve baseload capacity and lower costs.

positions.summary: Says he is in favor of expanding school choice, including private, charter, online, and homeschooling options, alongside public schools.
positions.quote: I am ardently in favor of expanding school choice to give parents the freedom to choose the best educational path for their children.

positions.summary: Supports an "all-of-the-above" energy approach using traditional and clean sources together and opposes what he calls the "Green New Deal movement," rather than a faster shift away from fossil fuels.
positions.quote: We do not have to choose between a clean environment and unleashing energy dominance; we must choose between a commonsense approach to energy policy or enabling the lucrative fearmongering of the Green New Deal movement.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means, the Committee on House Administration (Elections Subcommittee), and the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.

candidates.name: Raymond Smith Jr.
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 56.7% of the vote.
candidates.currentRole: Former North Carolina State Representative, District 21 (2019-2023)

summary.text: Raymond Smith Jr. is the Democratic nominee challenging incumbent Gregory Murphy in North Carolina's 3rd Congressional District. A Gulf War Army veteran, former educator, and transportation planner, he served on the Wayne County Board of Education and for two terms in the North Carolina House. His campaign website emphasizes rural healthcare, public education, and infrastructure.

background.text: Born and raised in Goldsboro, North Carolina, and a graduate of Goldsboro High School. According to his campaign website, his father served in the U.S. Marines and his mother served 18 years on the Wayne County School Board.
Served in the U.S. Army and Army Reserve; his campaign website describes him as a decorated Gulf War combat veteran and former military policeman.

Earned a bachelor's degree from North Carolina Agricultural and Technical State University (1992), a master's degree from North Carolina Central University (1998), and a Ph.D. from Fayetteville State University (2020). His campaign website lists the fields as supply chain management, public administration, and education leadership.

Worked as a teacher and football coach. According to his campaign website, he oversaw Wayne County's transition of paratransit service from private to local management and later worked as a statewide transportation planner for the North Carolina Department of Transportation.
Was elected in 2016 as the first African American at-large member of the Wayne County Board of Education, serving as vice chairman until 2019.

Served two terms in the North Carolina House of Representatives, District 21 (2019-2023), succeeding Larry Bell; committee work included Education, Local Government, Finance, Military and Veterans Affairs, Appropriations, and Transportation.
Was the Democratic candidate for North Carolina State Senate District 4 in 2024, losing the general election to incumbent Eldon Newton III.

Active as a trustee of St. James AME Zion Church and in the Omega Psi Phi Fraternity and Prince Hall Free and Accepted Masons; according to his campaign website, he lives in Goldsboro with his wife and family.

priorities.text: Investing in public schools, reducing class sizes, and supporting teachers with resources; providing equitable education for all students.
Economic development and job creation, including modernizing water, sewer and broadband infrastructure.
Quality, affordable healthcare and lower costs for working families.

positions.summary: Lists quality, affordable healthcare among his top campaign priorities.

record.text: Served two terms in the North Carolina House of Representatives representing District 21 (Wayne and Sampson counties), from January 2019 to January 2023, sitting on the Education-Community Colleges, Local Government, and Federal Relations committees.

candidates.researchNotes: Priorities are drawn from Smith's 2026 campaign website as summarized by Ballotpedia; his most recent full Candidate Connection survey dates to 2024, from his prior campaign.

candidates.name: Daniel Cavender
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from a canceled Libertarian Party primary.

summary.text: Daniel Cavender is the Libertarian Party nominee in North Carolina's 3rd Congressional District. He is a Marine Corps Reserve veteran and fire protection equipment technician who, in his 2024 Ballotpedia survey, described a pro-freedom platform including marijuana legalization and permitless gun carry. He ran as a Libertarian for the North Carolina State Senate in 2024.

background.text: Born in Lexington, North Carolina, and graduated from Central Davidson High School.
Served in the U.S. Marine Corps Reserve from 2015 to 2022.
Earned an associate degree from Davidson-Davie Community College (2019) and a bachelor's degree from the University of North Carolina Greensboro (2021).
Works as a fire protection equipment technician.
Ran for North Carolina State Senate District 30 in 2024 and lost the general election.
As of 2024, was affiliated with the Davidson County Libertarian Party, the Libertarian Party of North Carolina, and the American Legion.

priorities.text: Constitutional carry, opposing gun-law restrictions he views as infringements on the Second Amendment.

positions.summary: Says he believes all gun laws are infringements on the Second Amendment and supports constitutional carry.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions are drawn from Cavender's 2024 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, completed during a prior state legislative campaign; no updated 2026 survey or campaign website was located.
